subject.title: fix(security): bound plugin manifest reads in audit deep scan

question: Should deep audit enforce this 1 MiB package-manifest limit and accept directory-only fallback coverage when an installed plugin manifest exceeds it?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but the permanent byte threshold and accepted loss of manifest-declared forced-entry coverage define security policy that tests and repository history cannot choose.

options.title: Approve bounded policy
options.body: Keep the 1 MiB audit-specific limit and accept a visible warning plus best-effort directory scan for oversized manifests.

options.title: Align shared limit
options.body: Replace the local constant with an existing or newly centralized package-manifest limit before merge.

options.title: Require full coverage
options.body: Pause until a bounded parsing design can recover declared entrypoints without buffering the entire manifest.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded policy
recommendation.body: Keep the 1 MiB audit-specific limit and accept a visible warning plus best-effort directory scan for oversized manifests.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the scanner and added observable failure behavior, making them the strongest available owner for the fallback-policy decision.
